newsitem.title: USA: Morgan cut Gap due to sales outlook.
newsitem.headline: Morgan cut Gap due to sales outlook.

text.p: Morgan Stanley & Co analyst Sharon Pearson said Thursday she downgraded Gap Inc because she believed the retailer's sales gains will be weaker during the rest of the year than in the spring and summer.
Earlier, Morgan cut its rating on Gap to an outperform from a strong buy. Gap's stock was off 1-1/8 at 29-1/2.
The specialty retailer posted strong gains in same-store sales in March, April, May, June and July. But the momentum weakened in August when Gap's same-store sales were flat.
While Wall Street expects Gap's business to bounce back this fall, Pearson said she is not confident it will.
"The expectation is that the rebound will be there," she said. "Generally the feedback is September is so-so" for the retail industry as a whole.
Gap will release sales results for September in two weeks.

Since Gap's sales were fairly brisk last fall, it will be difficult to outpace those gains this year. That was not the case earlier this year. Gap's same-store sales rose nine percent during the first six months of 1996 compared to a three percent decline in the same period of 1995.
Pearson did not change her earnings estimates. She expects Gap to earn $1.54 a share this year and $1.75 next year. Gap had a profit of $1.23 in 1995, adjusted for a two-for-one stock split.
